findings.description: The instance user_data embeds long-lived AWS access key credentials (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) in a shell script stored in instance metadata, readable via the metadata service by anything able to reach the instance.

The security group allows ingress on TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration of the instance to the entire internet and enabling credential brute-force or exploitation of any SSH weakness.

The EBS volume has no encrypted attribute set, so data written to the attached disk is stored unencrypted at rest; combined with the public EC2 instance this increases exposure of any sensitive data on the volume.
The EBS snapshot is created without an encrypted attribute, so the snapshot of the server disk is stored unencrypted and can be shared or copied in cleartext form.
The bucket that receives VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, so flow log data is stored unencrypted in S3 despite containing network metadata.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched in this subnet, including the portal server, receives a public IP and is directly internet-reachable, expanding attack surface beyond the intended ingress rules.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes all instances launched in this subnet to receive public IP addresses, exposing them directly to the internet.
Egress is allowed to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports and protocols, giving the instance unrestricted outbound access that permits data exfiltration and remote command-and-control from a compromised host.
The user_data installs and starts Apache listening on port 80, which the security group exposes to 0.0.0.0/0, so all web traffic to the portal is transmitted unencrypted with no TLS termination.
